Destination Thailand Visa (DTV) documentation shape
value_raw: A bank balance of 500,000 THB held for at least 3 months before applying — cryptocurrency and investment-portfolio balances are explicitly not accepted — plus a clean immigration record, and the application must be filed from outside Thailand on the official e-Visa platform (which reportedly checks IP address and GPS data to enforce that rule). The remote-worker (Workcation) category then demands proof of ACTIVE work: an employment contract or employer letter explicitly authorizing remote work, or client contracts/invoices showing an ongoing income pattern over roughly 3-6 months, or business registration with revenue proof. Passive income alone (investment, dividend, savings-drawdown) is explicitly described as insufficient as primary proof — it can supplement active-income documentation but cannot substitute for it.

fact_label: O-A / O-X documentation shape
value_raw: One documentation row covering both tiers of this route. O-A (1-year): 800,000 THB held in a Thai bank account for at least 2 months before application (and not dropping below 400,000 THB during the visa year), OR a documented monthly income of at least 65,000 THB (typically evidenced by an embassy income affidavit), OR a combination of deposit plus annual income totaling 800,000 THB — plus mandatory health insurance from an insurer approved by Thailand's insurance regulator (OIC), minimum 40,000 THB outpatient / 400,000 THB inpatient annual coverage. O-X (5-10 year): a security deposit of at least 3,000,000 THB in a Thai bank. Ordinary pension/retirement/investment income is the accepted evidence class — no active-employment documentation standard exists on this route.

fact_label: O-A documentation shape
value_raw: 800,000 THB held in a Thai bank account for at least 2 months before application (balance can't drop below 400,000 THB during the visa year), OR a documented monthly income of at least 65,000 THB (typically evidenced by an embassy income affidavit), OR a combination of deposit plus annual income totaling 800,000 THB — plus mandatory health insurance from an insurer approved by Thailand's insurance regulator (OIC), minimum 40,000 THB outpatient / 400,000 THB inpatient annual coverage. Ordinary pension/retirement/investment income is the accepted evidence class — no active-employment documentation standard exists on this route.

fact_label: O-X documentation shape
value_raw: A security deposit of at least 3,000,000 THB held in a Thai bank account. Ordinary pension/retirement/investment income is the accepted evidence class — no active-employment documentation standard exists on this route. This tier additionally carries its own 14-country eligible-nationality list, gated separately — see TH:o-x-nationality-restriction.

fact_label: Long-Term Resident (LTR) Wealthy Pensioner documentation shape
value_raw: Proof of passive income at the category's bar — pension, rental, or dividend income are the named qualifying classes — or the reduced income bar paired with evidence of a Thailand-based investment of at least USD 250,000. Cross-category financial-security requirement rides on top: health insurance with at least USD 50,000 of coverage, or a minimum USD 100,000 balance in savings/checking as the alternative.

fact_label: Long-Term Resident (LTR) Wealthy Global Citizen documentation shape
value_raw: Evidence of USD 1 million+ in total assets, including at least USD 500,000 held in specific Thai assets — an asset-portfolio documentation burden, not an income-stream one; the previously-required USD 80,000 annual income floor for this category is reported removed. Cross-category financial-security requirement rides on top: health insurance with at least USD 50,000 of coverage, or a minimum USD 100,000 balance in savings/checking as the alternative.

fact_label: Long-Term Resident (LTR) Work-from-Thailand Professional documentation shape
value_raw: Income documentation at the category's bar plus employer-side corporate proof: the remote employer must be a publicly listed company, or a private firm with at least 3 years of operations and USD 50 million+ in annual revenue — a documentation burden built for an employee of a large company, which a solo freelancer or passive-income applicant cannot assemble regardless of income level. Cross-category financial-security requirement rides on top: health insurance with at least USD 50,000 of coverage, or a minimum USD 100,000 balance in savings/checking as the alternative.

fact_label: Thailand Privilege Visa documentation shape
value_raw: A one-time membership payment for the chosen tier is the entire financial qualification — no income proof, no asset proof, no ongoing financial test of any kind, active or passive. The documentation burden is essentially the purchase itself, which is why this is the one Thai route where the income-type question does not arise at all.
